challenge.better_approach: Considered: keep the prose slug and add a separate title field for listings. Rejected: the listing he described is the file list itself (date + text), so only the name fixes what he sees. Considered: drop the title from the contract and keep prose naming. Rejected: prose's first words are often filler ('well only one box hex even has'), which is the measured symptom. This is the smallest change: one argument to slug_of, one field in the record.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no reader re-derives an idea's id from its prose. slug_of's docstring argues the id should be guessable from the prose so a human gets it right; with a title the author chose, it is guessable from the title instead. Must be checked at /sorted by grepping every caller of slug_of and every reader of ideas/ ids (skill_block, operator_inbox, question, probes).
challenge.prior_art: Consulted the congruency lab copy of skills/idea's charter: input_contract.title already exists and says it makes 'every artifact identifiable at a glance', so the intent was always there and the code stopped short; this completes it rather than adding anything new. Ticket 1baf0b52b218 (an-idea-has-an-address) arms the pickup watch over CairnCommons/ideas/ against from_idea; it reads ids, not how they were derived. Tickets in the commons name themselves from a title slug already (e.g. 1baf0b52b218-an-idea-has-an-address), so this matches the house convention.
challenge.real_collision: With slug_of's docstring rationale ('an id a human cannot guess from the prose is an id a human will get wrong'): a distinction, not exclusive — the aim, a guessable deterministic id, holds better from an author-chosen title than from the first seven words of verbatim prose. No Law or decision collides; Akien's word outranks the docstring (Law 9).

answers.falsifier: Done when an idea fired with title 'cortical column network strategies' lands at CairnCommons/ideas/<date>-cortical-column-network-strategies.json carrying `title`, proven by the door's own proof red-first. Wrong intent if Akien, listing ideas, still reads the slug as something other than the title, or if any reader resolves from_idea by re-deriving the slug from prose (then the id derivation is load-bearing elsewhere and this breaks it).
answers.from_idea: none, because Akien stated it as a correction on 2026-11-23 while the idea at /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/ideas/2026-11-23-cortical-column-network-strategies.json was being renamed by hand; the defect is in /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/skills/idea/door.py
answers.how: In skills/idea/door.py, build the record's stem from slug_of(payload['title']) instead of slug_of(payload['prose']) and write `title` into the record beside `prose`; keep the date prefix and the collision suffix. Extend proofs/test_idea_door.py: the record's id and file name derive from the title, and the record carries it. Charter input_contract.title stops saying it 'rides the berth' and says it names the record. Existing records keep their names (no migration): they are addresses /intent's from_idea may already cite.
traces_to: Law 1 — the door already asks for the title and then discards it, so a human re-derives the name by hand (measured 2026-11-23: one idea renamed by hand)
Law 5 — the record carries what a reader listing ideas needs now: what each one is
Law 9 — Akien's correction of the artifact: 'that text, in a list of such tickets, IS the title'
answers.what: An idea's commons record is named from the title its author gave it, and carries that title, because in a list of ideas the date plus that name IS the title.

bullets.text: Akien 2026-11-23: 'that first few words becomes the title from the point of view of i'm looking at these things marked ideas and it's a number plus some text. that text, in a list of such tickets, IS the title.'

Measured: the idea door refuses a packet without `title`, then names the commons record from slug_of(prose) and drops the title; it survives only in the instance-space berth. First casualty: 2026-11-23-well-only-one-box-hex-even-has, renamed by hand to 2026-11-23-cortical-column-network-strategies (commons 63d42b0f9).
